How do volcanoes appear

Pin Wall storyboard, 11 s, five beats. One wall of pins, one continuous camera crane. Each still is the real scene at that beat, rendered with the stage kit.

Beat 10.0 – 2.4 sstill at 1.2 s
On-screen text
ROCK MELTS DEEP UNDERGROUND  |  magma: 700–1,300 °C
What changes
Start state. Flat slate-blue plain of pins. An orange glow fades up under the pins, as if seen through the crust. Faint tremor rings run out across the plain every 0.7 s.
Camera
Low pass across the pin heads, shallow focus, drifting left and slowly rising.
Sounds
Room bed, thousands of pin ticks, deep rumble starts to swell, a soft thud for each tremor ring.
Beat 22.4 – 4.7 sstill at 4.4 s
On-screen text
MAGMA GATHERS AND SWELLS THE GROUND
What changes
Same wall. The glow pulls in toward one spot and brightens. The ground there swells into a dome about 1.25 units high and shivers. Three glowing cracks open across the top.
Camera
Keeps rising and turns toward the dome; focus pulls onto it.
Sounds
Rumble climbs in pitch and level, tremor thuds come closer together, crackle ticks as cracks open, a short riser into the break.
Beat 34.7 – 6.5 sstill at 5.4 s
On-screen text
IT BREAKS THROUGH
What changes
At 4.8 s the dome bursts. The top drops into a crater, the first layer of rock runs down the flanks, lava bombs fly up and fall back, a shock ring crosses the plain and ash pales the pins near the vent.
Camera
Continuous crane, now high enough that the whole cone and the ring read.
Sounds
Big impact with sub drop, noise blast, a cloud of pin ticks, whoosh following the ring, small plinks as bombs land.
Beat 46.5 – 9.0 sstill at 7.6 s
On-screen text
LAVA AND ASH PILE UP, LAYER BY LAYER
What changes
Two more eruptions (6.6 s and 8.2 s). Each adds a layer to the cone, sends another ring out, and runs glowing lava down five channels. The lava cools to a pale crust behind the front.
Camera
Drifting round to a three-quarter view; the cone fills the middle of the frame.
Sounds
Impact per eruption, lava hiss under each flow, tick bursts thinning out as each layer settles.
Beat 59.0 – 11.0 sstill at 10.6 s
On-screen text
A VOLCANO  |  built by many eruptions
What changes
Result. A finished cone with a glowing crater and cooling lava ribs. Everything finished stands still; the crater keeps glowing. Holds for the last second.
Camera
Ends on a raised three-quarter view of the whole relief, then holds.
Sounds
One low warm note (D3 + A3), a single bell, the room bed carries on. A small silence just before it.

Assumed facts and choices

  • Magma temperature, 700–1,300 °C: the usual textbook range (cooler silica-rich magma to hot basalt). It is the only number on screen.
  • The glow under the plain is a diagram, not a cross-section: pins light up as if the heat shows through the crust. Plate tectonics (where most volcanoes form: plate edges and hot spots) is not shown. Say if you want a beat for it.
  • Colours: slate blue = ground, warm tan = new rock, pale grey-lilac = ash and cooled crust, orange = lava.
  • Three eruptions (4.8, 6.6, 8.2 s) build a cone about 3.4 units tall. Shape and timing are schematic, not to scale.
  • Total length 11 s, 5 captions, each one short line on the screwed plate at the bottom.
  • Stills are 1280×720 with only 5 samples in software GL (no GPU here), so depth of field and soft shadows look grainier than the final will. They come from the real scene code, not a block-out.
  • I used the repo copies of the stage and sound kits and did not diff them against your paste. Oswald and Inter are loaded locally for the stills; the final page uses Google Fonts.

Say OK or send changes (captions, beats, colours, length). Then I build the full animation with sound.
